description: High-Resolution LiDAR Point Clouds for Arctic Road Infrastructure Analytics Leveraging Machine Learning: Geospatial Data from the Dalton Highway, Alaska, (Yukon River Camp - Finger Mountain) August 2024 is a data set deposited in UC Santa Barbara by its authors Emmanuel Chukwuemeka, Timothy Pasch. Remote sensing makes it possible to gather data rapidly, accurately, and non-destructively, allowing for access to remote areas in near real-time. LiDAR sensor data were collected along Alaska's Dalton Highway as part of continued efforts to provide more geospatial data in Arctic regions relevant to cold region research. Coverage: the Dalton Highway, Alaska. Formats: XML. It is reached through its DOI or landing page, listed on this page. Access is free of charge and open according to the repository. The licence is not stated (no licence in the DataCite metadata read on 2026-09-29). Caveats: written from the DataCite metadata (title, abstract, subjects and rights) read on 2026-09-29; the deposit itself was not opened or downloaded, so its contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet for this repository.
